sources.title: Annette Schmiedchen, Buddhist Endowments by Śaiva Kings under the Maitrakas (2021)
sources.note: Original Endowment Studies 5, pp. 107-134, DOI 10.1163/24685968-05010002; full paper read through author-upload text. Publisher PDF fetch failed. Pp. 114-117 support cisterns, wells, religious affiliation, provisions and repairs.

sources.title: Annette Schmiedchen, Monastic Complexes for Monks and Nuns (2021-22)
sources.note: Original Buddhism, Law and Society 7, pp. 59-98, directly readable full article. Pp. 61-62 plates and seals; pp. 67-71 founders; abstract and nunneries discussion. Dudda was a laywoman and her foundation housed monks; she is not called a nun here.

sources.title: DHARMA, Palitana plates of Dhruvasena I, year 206
sources.note: Direct digital edition by Annette Schmiedchen. Edition line 1 has svasti valabhītaḥ after a spiral sign. The sample omits the sign rather than equating it with Oṃ. Sanskrit normalized into modern Devanagari; historical letter forms are not reproduced.

sources.title: Sten Konow, Palitana plates of Dhruvasena I, translation in Siddham
sources.note: Direct full translation from Epigraphia Indica XI, pp. 108-109. Lines 1, 10-25 and 28-30 checked. Date stated as Valabhi year 206 and sixth century to avoid conversion ambiguity.

sources.title: Xuanzang, The Great Tang Dynasty Record of the Western Regions, translated by Li Rongxi
sources.note: Direct BDK translation, online printed pp. 301-303 / PDF pages 317-319, Fascicle XI, Valabhi and Suratta. Counts and royal charity are attributed to the traveler. His moral stereotypes and religious miracle narratives are not adopted.

sources.title: National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities, Vallabhipur shell bangle UM-MSU-GJ-410140
sources.note: Original indexed M. S. University, Baroda collection record read in full. Reproducible query: "nmma" "VALLABHIPUR" "grooved". Direct detail page failed. Maitraka classification, shell material, grooved polished fragment and excavation provenance are explicit.

sources.note: Original indexed collection record read in full; direct detail page failed. Query: site:nmma.nic.in/nmma/antiqDetail.do "VALLABHIPUR" "Stone bead". Maitraka, pale white stone, central perforation, smoothed surface. Inconsistent measurements and depth formatting are excluded.

proposedOverrides.name: Maitrakas of Valabhi
proposedOverrides.summary: Valabhi’s western Indian kingdom supported trade, learned monasteries and practical endowments. This map selects its late phase.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One exact indexed record. No alias, new geography or runtime replacement. The full historical dynasty is contextualized while retaining imported 700-800 map coverage.
limitations: The decoded western Indian polygon reaches beyond the securely described Kathiawar-centred core; opening explicitly qualifies its frontier.
Copper-plate and traveler evidence from the sixth and seventh centuries deliberately supplies earlier dynasty context; this is not dated to 700 by interpolation.
No universal school attendance, city-wide hospital or sanitation network is inferred.
Valabhi year 206 is left as a named era plus sixth century, avoiding unsupported precise CE conversion.
Final fall and destruction dates vary; ending is uncertain, not a fabricated event at 800.
